edition.name: Migne PL 4 (1844), Ep. LXIV, via Corpus Corporum / Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Nec mirum si consilia nostra aut Domini praecepta nunc abnuunt qui Dominnm negaverunt: stipes et oblationes et lucra desiderant, quibus prius insatiabiles incubabant; et coenis atque epulis etiam nunc inhiant, quarum crapulam superstite nuper in dies cruditate ructabant, nunc manifestissime comprobantes nec ante se religioni, sed ventri potius et quaestui profana cupiditate servisse. Unde et ipsam venisse perspicimus et credimus de Dei exploratione censuram, ne apud altare consistere et contrectare ulterius perseverarent pudorem incesti, fidem perfidi, religionem profani, divina terreni, sancta sacrilegi. Quod ne tales ad altaris impiamenta et contagia fratrum denuo redeant, omnibus viribus excubandum est, et omni vigore nitendum ut quantum possumus ab hac eos sui sceleris audacia retundamus, ne adhuc agere pro sacerdote conentur qui ad mortis extrema dejecti, ultra lapsos laicos ruinae majoris pondere proruerunt.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is it a wonder if they now reject our plans or the Lord's precepts, who have denied the Lord: they desire fees and offerings and profits, with which they previously were insatiable; and they even now pant after dinners and feasts, the gluttony of which, while they recently survived, they belched out in crude daily fashion, now most clearly proving that they served not religion before, but rather their belly and gain with profane desire. Whence we also perceive and believe that a censure has come from God's examination, lest they continue to stand at the altar and further handle the shame of incest, the faith of the perfidious, the religion of the profane, the divine things of the earthly, the holy things of the sacrilegious. So that such people may not return again to the impious desecrations and contaminations of the brothers at the altar, it must be watched over with all strength and striven for with all vigor, so that as much as we can, we may repel them from the audacity of their own crime, lest they attempt to act as a priest, who, having been cast down to the extreme of death, have fallen beyond the fallen laity with the weight of greater ruin.
pass_b_english: It is no wonder that they now reject our plans or the Lord's commandments, since they have denied the Lord. They crave fees, offerings, and profits, wallowing in them with the same insatiable greed as before. Even now they pant after dinners and feasts; they used to belch out the gluttony of those banquets in crude daily fashion, and now they prove most clearly that they served not religion before, but rather their belly and their gain with profane desire. We perceive and believe that a censure has come from God's scrutiny, lest they persist in standing at the altar and further handling the shame of incest, the faith of the perfidious, the religion of the profane, divine things as earthly, and holy things as sacrilegious. So that such people may not return again to the impious desecrations and contaminations of the brothers at the altar, we must stand guard with all our strength and strive with all our vigor to repel them, as far as we can, from the audacity of their own crime, lest they attempt to act as priests—men who, having been cast down to the very brink of death, have fallen beyond the fallen laity under the weight of a greater ruin.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent in meaning. Pass B's slight stylistic expansion ('wallowing in them with the same insatiable greed as before') is a valid rendering of 'quibus prius insatiabiles incubabant'. The translation of 'divina terreni, sancta sacrilegi' as 'divine things as earthly, and holy things as sacrilegious' in Pass B correctly captures the implied comparison/substitution in the Latin.

source: 'stipes et oblationes et lucra desiderant, quibus prius insatiabiles incubabant'; English: 'They crave fees, offerings, and profits, wallowing in them with the same insatiable greed as before.'
